summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recurrent UTIs due to urethral diverticulum was readmitted one day after discharge due to recurrent abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She also reported acute left flank pain, which resolved overnight. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and pain control. Metoclopramide was discontinued due to lack of efficacy, and promethazine was initiated as an alternative. A urine culture showed no growth, but a short course of Bactrim was prescribed given her history of UTIs triggering gastroparesis. She improved rapidly, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and strong recommendations for follow-up with gastroenterology and primary care. Plans were made to evaluate the possibility of a port for future access.
